html:
The Santiam were a band of the Kalapuya people who lived along the Santiam River in the Willamette Valley of Oregon. They spoke a dialect of Central Kalapuya.

Like other Kalapuya bands, they dug camas roots, gathered acorns, hunted deer, and burned the valley grasslands each year to keep them open. Disease in the 1830s hit them hard, just before settlers came down the Oregon Trail to farm the valley. In 1855 the Kalapuya signed away the valley by treaty and were moved to the Grand Ronde reservation. Their descendants belong to the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde. See also Chemapho.
